To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the storage of plant samples as tissue or as tissue extracts affects enzyme activities.
storage duration and temperature affect the activities of ascorbate per-oxidase (APX), glutathione re-ductase (GR), and superoxide dis-mutase (SOD) in rice tissue.
storage duration and temperature affect enzyme activity in rice extracts and that enzyme-specific storage methods are needed to obtain reliable data for enzyme kinetics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of different extraction and storage methods on the activity of antioxidant enzymes.
the effect of storage methods on the activity of enzymes in extracts of fresh tissue samples and of extracts stored at −20 ° C or −80 ° C.
the effects of different storage conditions and durations on the activity of enzymes known as antioxidants in rice tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
enzyme activity measurements from stored plant material are possible but should not be used for comparative purposes between genotypes or treatments.
enzyme activities are affected by different storage methods and durations and that these effects are strongly enzyme specific.
enzyme activities in extracts from stored rice tissue samples can be used for comparative studies of the same enzyme and tissue type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the storage of tissue samples is a good option for the enzymes studied here, while the storage of enzyme extracts is not recommended.
the enzyme activities are strongly dependent upon the storage method, storage time, and storage temperature.
enzyme activities in plant tissues can be stored at −20 ° C, but that enzyme extracts can be stored at 4 °C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
enzyme activity can be maintained in extracts from stored tissue for a few weeks.
storage methods and storage duration should be carefully considered and optimized when working with large numbers of tissue or extracts from tissue.

the storage of tissue samples and the storage duration and storage temperature of enzyme extracts have a strong effect on the measured activity of the enzymes ascorbate peroxide, glutathione peroxidase, and super oxide dismutase.
